scope_note: This is the generation-7 corrective pass responding to the independent reviewer's second rejection of PR #5620 (this exact branch head), which reproduced 9 concrete defects against live isolated PostgreSQL and a strict signed JWT. Each is fixed with real code changes: (1) JWT sub/tenant claim normalization — service.py's auth path now strips whitespace and rejects (403) a JWT whose sub or a tenant claim name is present but blank/whitespace-only after stripping (new _reject_malformed_identity_claims, run before _require_verified_identity/_reject_reserved_tenant_claim/any persistence); _reject_reserved_tenant_claim and _caller_tenant now strip before comparing/persisting, so a whitespace-padded '__builtin__' claim is still caught and a legitimate tenant claim's surrounding whitespace never leaks into owner_tenant. (2) StrategySpec validation bypasses closed on both routes — the generic POST /api/registry/entries route now requires lineage, an embedded strategy_id match, and (via a new register_entry closure) runs the same _validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage sequence check as the dedicated route whenever a full StrategySpec is embedded under metadata.strategy_spec, closing the 9.9.9-version-jump-with-mismatched-embedded-strategy_id-and-empty-lineage/checksum bypass; the dedicated POST /api/registry/strategy-specs facade (_strategy_spec_register_payload) now also treats a metadata-embedded strategy_spec (including {}) as real content requiring schema validation, closing the empty-spec-with-arbitrary-checksum bypass. (3) idempotency-key create replay now compares a request fingerprint — PostgresRegistryStore.create_with_receipt / RegistryStore.create_with_receipt (storage.py) and RegistryService.register_with_idempotency now accept a request_fingerprint (the caller's normalized request body, computed before the factory ever runs, since the factory's own output embeds a fresh random identity on every call and cannot be compared across replays); a same Idempotency-Key reused with a different request now raises DivergentCommandReplayError -> 409, instead of silently returning the original entry. (4) StrategySpec revision creation is now bound to a per-strategy_id Postgres advisory transaction lock — new PostgresRegistryStore.register_strategy_spec_revision / RegistryStore.register_strategy_spec_revision / RegistryService.register_strategy_spec_revision take the lock, re-read the true latest-committed StrategySpec set under it, and re-run the version/lineage invariant (_check_strategy_spec_version_lineage, factored out of the old ctx-scoped pre-check) against that fresh read before inserting — the POST /api/registry/strategy-specs route now uses this atomic path instead of a separate unlocked pre-check followed by register_if_absent, closing the TOCTOU window where two concurrent next-version requests could each validate against the same stale 'latest' and both commit. (5) advance_artifact_state now has its own command-receipt/CAS, mirroring update_metadata's commit_metadata_cas — new PostgresRegistryStore.commit_artifact_state_cas / RegistryStore.commit_artifact_state_cas commit the artifact_state mutation and its command_key-scoped receipt in one Postgres transaction; the transition-legality/lineage business-rule check is now a validate() callback invoked by the store only on the genuinely-fresh (non-replay) path, so a replay never re-runs it against the entry's already-post-transition current state (which would otherwise spuriously raise 'forbidden transition'); this is documented explicitly as NOT a separate outbox in services/registry/contract.md's new 'Command-receipt durability mechanism' section and in first_release_contract.json's advance_artifact_state entry, replacing the prior generation's honest-but-now-stale 'no outbox/protocol/proof' claim. (6) strategy_adapter.py's update_params now performs a pre-mutation owner GET that verifies the caller-supplied registry_id actually belongs to the requested strategy_id BEFORE issuing the mutating PATCH (previously this was only discovered from the PATCH's own response, after a possibly-partial mutation), and captures that pre-issue snapshot (registry_id/checksum/version/owner_tenant) as the immutable identity baseline for (7). (7) the same pre-issue baseline is now used to verify every subsequent response (replay, response-lost/ambiguous, and normal-success paths) via a new _diverges_from_original check, instead of trusting a replay response's self-reported strategy_id alone or comparing against a fresh, possibly-since-mutated 'current' GET — closing the fault-injection gap where a replay response reporting the right strategy_id but a forged registry_id/checksum/version was previously accepted. (8) main.py's /readyz registry_owner dependency probe now queries the actual configured owner table (SELECT 1 FROM <table> LIMIT 0) instead of a bare SELECT 1, so a missing/unbootstrapped schema (e.g. REGISTRY_STORE_BOOTSTRAP=0 against a schema that was never created) now fails closed (ready=false) instead of reporting ready=true while every real entry read/write raises psycopg's InvalidSchemaName; storage.py's backend-selection fail-closed behavior (DSN-configured-without-explicit-postgres-backend, enforced-posture-without-explicit-backend) was already present from an earlier pass and is unchanged. (9) foundation/postgres_json_store.py's bootstrap() now takes a session-scoped Postgres advisory transaction lock (keyed on the table name, via a new PostgresJsonOwnerStore.advisory_xact_lock helper) around the whole CREATE SCHEMA + CREATE TABLE sequence, so two fresh processes racing their first bootstrap serialize instead of both attempting concurrent DDL; the existing exception-based fallback was also widened from catching only 23505 (unique_violation) to also catching 42P07 (duplicate_table/duplicate_object) as a belt-and-suspenders measure, per the reviewer's explicit preference for the lock as the primary fix.

summary: service.py: new _reject_malformed_identity_claims (finding 1); _reject_reserved_tenant_claim/_caller_tenant/_actor_context now strip claim values before comparing/persisting; _resolve_entry_or_draft_payload's STRATEGY_SPEC branch enforces embedded-strategy_id match + lineage + checksum-binding when metadata.strategy_spec is present (finding 2); register_entry threads a request_fingerprint into register_with_idempotency and, for a generic-route full StrategySpec, calls _validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage before persisting (findings 2/3); _strategy_spec_register_payload now treats a metadata-embedded strategy_spec (including {}) as real content requiring schema validation (finding 2); _validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage split into a pure _check_strategy_spec_version_lineage(existing_entries, ...) plus a ctx-scoped pre-check wrapper and a _strategy_spec_lineage_validator closure builder, both consumed by RegistryService.register_strategy_spec_revision (finding 4); register_strategy_spec route now calls register_strategy_spec_revision instead of a separate pre-check + register_if_absent; AdvanceRequest gained an optional command_key field threaded through all four advance routes, and those routes (plus update_deployment_summary) now catch RegistryConflictError -> 409 explicitly instead of falling through to the generic RegistryError -> 400 handler (finding 5).

split_api.py: new RegistryService.register_strategy_spec_revision (finding 4) delegating to the store's per-strategy_id-locked variant; RegistryService.register_with_idempotency accepts request_fingerprint and maps DivergentCommandReplayError -> RegistryConflictError (finding 3); RegistryService.advance_artifact_state accepts command_key, moves the transition-legality/lineage check into a _validate_transition callback invoked by the store only on the non-replay path, and maps DivergentCommandReplayError -> RegistryConflictError (finding 5).

storage.py / pg_store.py: create_with_receipt (both backends) accepts request_fingerprint, computes a digest before the factory runs, and rejects a same-command_key/different-fingerprint replay (finding 3); new register_strategy_spec_revision (both backends) — Postgres takes a per-strategy_id pg_advisory_xact_lock and re-reads/re-validates under it before inserting; the in-memory backend's existing process-wide lock provides the same serialization (finding 4); new commit_artifact_state_cas (both backends), mirroring commit_metadata_cas, with a validate callback invoked only on the non-replay path and a request digest that deliberately excludes the entry's current artifact_state (which legitimately differs between the original call and a later replay) (finding 5).

command_adapters/strategy_adapter.py: _execute_update_params now performs a pre-mutation owner GET (before the PATCH) that verifies registry_id belongs to strategy_id and captures the pre-issue immutable baseline (registry_id/checksum/version/owner_tenant) (finding 6); a new _diverges_from_original check is applied to the replay, response-lost, and normal-success response paths, binding all three to that pre-issue baseline instead of trusting a response's self-reported strategy_id or comparing against a possibly-since-mutated fresh GET (finding 7).

test_service.py: added regression tests for whitespace sub/tenant claim rejection and whitespace-padded reserved-tenant rejection (finding 1); generic-route embedded-StrategySpec lineage requirement and version-sequence enforcement, and dedicated-route empty-metadata-strategy_spec rejection (finding 2); Idempotency-Key divergent-request 409 (finding 3); advance command_key replay-returns-original-receipt and divergent-replay-409 (finding 5).

test_owner_durability.py: added test_readyz_fails_closed_when_owner_schema_is_missing, reproducing the exact bootstrap=0/missing-schema scenario against real Postgres and asserting /readyz reports ready=false (finding 8).

test_registry_owner_transaction.py: added test_concurrent_strategy_spec_revision_registration_serializes_not_races, a real-Postgres two-thread race proving the advisory-lock-serialized read-validate-write never lets a stale revision commit after a later, no-longer-compatible one already has (finding 4). This test's first version determined 'which attempt committed first/second' by sorting committed rows on the entries table's `updated_at` column and initially FAILED an independent re-run of this exact head (both 1.0.1 and 2.0.0 committed, correctly, but sorted in the wrong order) — root cause was that Postgres' `now()` (used as `updated_at`'s default) reflects each transaction's *start* time, not its commit time, so the attempt that blocks longest on the advisory lock can still have the earlier `updated_at` even though it commits second; this made the assertion's ordering non-deterministic under lock contention, not the advisory-lock fix itself broken. Replaced the ordering source with a Python-side `completion_order` list appended to (under a `threading.Lock`) immediately after each thread's `register_strategy_spec_revision` call returns (i.e. after that thread's transaction has actually committed and released the advisory lock) — this reflects true real-world completion order. Re-ran 5x after the fix: 1 passed each run.

test_strategy_registry_owner_prerequisite.py: updated every update_params test to account for the new pre-mutation identity-verification GET (now the first of 2-3 HTTP calls depending on path); added test_update_params_replay_with_forged_registry_id_is_rejected_despite_matching_strategy_id proving a replay response with the right strategy_id but a wrong registry_id/checksum is rejected (finding 7); test_update_params_rejects_registry_id_belonging_to_different_strategy now additionally asserts the mismatch is caught by the pre-check GET alone (mock_http.call_count == 1, no PATCH issued) (finding 6).

not_covered_in_this_delivery: The reviewer's finding 5 language ('atomic state/original receipt/outbox or documented recoverable protocol and crash-window proof') is addressed as a same-transaction command-receipts row for advance_artifact_state (mirroring the pre-existing update_metadata_cas mechanism), documented explicitly as NOT a separate outbox in contract.md. No test in this pass kills a live server process mid-transaction to observe the crash-window property directly (as test_owner_durability_real_process.py already does for register/restart and two-process CAS/replay) — the atomicity is proven by direct assertion against the shared-transaction store methods (both entry and receipt rows land together, verified via test_metadata_cas_commit_and_receipt_are_one_atomic_transaction's pattern for metadata, and via the new advance command_key tests at the HTTP layer for artifact_state), not by an actual process-kill experiment for the advance path specifically.

strategy_adapter.py's readback/replay verification is bound to a pre-issue GET snapshot (registry_id/checksum/version/owner_tenant) captured by the adapter itself immediately before issuing the PATCH, not to a dedicated server-side 'original command receipt' fetched by command_key — the Registry does not currently expose an HTTP endpoint to read back a specific command_receipts row by its scoped key, only the mutable entry itself. This closes the concrete fault-injection scenario reproduced (wrong registry_id/checksum/version accepted despite matching strategy_id) but does not bind verification to the *actor* of the original command (last_actor is legitimately mutable on every write, including the PATCH itself, so it cannot serve as an immutable comparison field without that new endpoint).

review.decision: This branch head was rejected a second time (generation-7 rejection) with 9 concrete, live-PostgreSQL-reproduced defects across auth-claim normalization, StrategySpec validation bypasses (both routes), idempotency-key request comparison, a StrategySpec revision-creation TOCTOU race, missing advance_artifact_state receipts, BFF adapter identity/replay verification ordering, readiness-probe schema verification, and a Postgres bootstrap DDL race under concurrent fresh-process startup. This revision implements real fixes for all 9, verified against a live isolated PostgreSQL instance available in this session (not skipped), with the honest residual gaps recorded above (no crash-mid-transaction process-kill proof specifically for the advance path; no dedicated server-side command-receipt-by-key read endpoint for the BFF adapter to bind against, so its replay verification uses a pre-issue GET snapshot instead). Pending independent re-review; no reuse of any prior approval.
